Actually, congressional term limits would open up more opportunities for state legislators to move “up” so they have an incentive to support those limits.  Plus it’s popular with voters so why not get on the right side of the issue?


WeThePeople (@gallusmimsy)

Nobody in government is ever going to vote for term limits.  Not at the state level, and not at the federal level. Why would they? It’s literally a career ender.



— https://nitter.net/gallusmimsy/status/2056702871450566870#m

Article V doesn’t require Congress.  It is a state-driven process, just as the Founders intended in these situations.


Valspar11 (@Valspar111)

Yes. How do you plan to get that around the people that currently hold office and will NEVER make either of those things happen?



— https://nitter.net/Valspar111/status/2056698556208017589#m

Term limits and a balanced budget amendment would change the incentive structure for Congress in a positive way.  

We’ll never fix the mess otherwise.


Peter Lewis (@creathir)

💯 needs to happen. 

This with term limits has to take place, and the establishment political party has taken us SO FAR from what the founding fathers intended…

We need @COSProject , FAST!



— https://nitter.net/creathir/status/2056690571205308877#m

Gloating about people’s jobs getting wiped out and championing sticking people on government checks for subsistence… yeah, not hard to see why many would not look favorably on that.


Chief_Engineer (@ChiefEngineerCE)

They have offered zero value proposition for implementation. 

It's all - 

'Hey Tech bros are going to get incredibly rich and powerful while everyone loses their job!- isn't that great?'

Or 

'We need to make everyone unemployed before China does.'



— https://nitter.net/Chief

One reason why I support using Article V to add a balanced budget requirement to the Constitution.  We have only been able to get away with this so far because the US is the reserve currency.  The incentives need to change.
Not surprising.

Police Interceptor for the win.

80s Nostalgia Channel (@80s_channel)

All of them …





— https://nitter.net/80s_channel/status/2056333855104094224#m

The number of doomsday predictions made over the past 40 years that have now been proven false is significant.

Has media who amplified these predictions ever followed up and acknowledged pushing a false narrative?


Kyle Smith (@rkylesmith)

Al Gore predicted in 1992 that in the next few decades, Florida would lose 60 percent of its population due to climate change. 
Florida’s population is more than quadruple what he predicted it would be.





— https://nitter.net/rkylesmith/status/2056383847

You mean like we’ve been doing for years at record conservation levels?




79Vision (@79Visionz)

How bout we bring back the cowboys and all the ranchers that disappeared over the last few decades. What we even doing? Quit fucking building ugly ass apartments and subdivisions.
